description: Audit ledger populated from this session's actual tasks. This JSON is an audit record, NOT an atomic OS lock and NOT a scheduler. See gpu_lock_mechanism for what actually serialised GPU work.
lead_owner: HeheBoiz (single human lead; integrated and pushed every commit)

resource_policy.budget_reason_and_evidence: AGENTS.md allocates half the box to CIR; the other 10 threads serve a second project. Enforced by exporting WORKBENCH_BLAS_THREADS=8, WORKBENCH_DECODE_WORKERS=8, WORKBENCH_SCORE_THREADS=8 on every evaluation, with runner.BLAS_THREADS_PINNED=1 read back and verified at scoring time. Aggregate stayed within 10: 8 decode workers + torch intra-op pinned to 8 + BLAS 1 during scoring.
resource_policy.gpu_lock_mechanism: NO dedicated GPU lock file was used for cross-agent serialisation. Two DIFFERENT mechanisms were in play and they must not be confused. (1) WITHIN a process, run_composition takes a real fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on <artifacts>/composition/runs/<run_id>/.<model_id>_<checkpoint_id>.lock (runner.py:86-99, acquired at :1633) — this genuinely serialises model work against another workbench process touching the same run. (2) ACROSS the session's agents, serialisation was PROCESS-LEVEL ONLY: the GPU lane ran one composition_eval at a time and verified emptiness with pgrep -af composition_eval before each launch. That is a convention plus a check, not a lock: two agents calling pgrep in the same instant would both see nothing and both launch. Recorded as a deviation, not as a guarantee.
resource_policy.evaluator_serialisation_evidence: pgrep -af 'composition_eval|pytest workbench/tests' returned empty immediately before every sweep launch (four sweeps today) and before every model run; each sweep was launched only after the previous one exited.

deviations.what: Four lanes ran concurrently against a documented cap of three (max_concurrent_subagents: 3).
deviations.evidence: Lane A (evaluator fixes), Lane B (frontend light workspace), Lane C (checkpoint mapping), Lane D (model inventory) were all active in the same window; commits 7ef4cc4, f6796b3, 87ff419 and the inventory evidence pack landed while the GPU lane was producing run 30f6de42 and later. The GPU lane itself was a fifth concurrent actor.
deviations.impact: CPU contention contaminated every wall-time figure taken before ~09:20. Every RUN_LOG.csv row is labelled 'not_measured (concurrent load)' and G8 is NOT_RUN for this reason. No scientific result depends on those durations.
deviations.status: ACCEPTED_AND_RECORDED — not remediated; the shared worktree made serialisation impractical mid-session and the affected numbers are labelled.

deviations.what: The GPU lane took no timing measurements for most of the session.
deviations.evidence: RUN_LOG.csv throughput column reads 'not_measured (concurrent load)' for all 8 rows; gpu_peak_vram_mib is 'not_sampled (no sampler wired for this run)' for hint, ptha_mtst and tme, and a hand-observed value for limn (logs/limn.vram.observed.txt, explicitly labelled not-a-sampler).
deviations.impact: Required outcome #4 (measured wall-time improvement) is UNMET; G8 remains NOT_RUN. This is a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight: a baseline taken while three other lanes were compiling and running pytest would have been false, and the handoff's own rule (§A) forbids it.
deviations.status: DEFERRED — harness prepared (perf_bench.py), measurement pending an idle box.

deviations.evidence: RUN_LOG.csv conesep row originally said 'bit-identical' while quoting a gap that differed; per-query diff showed 17/18009 ranks moved. Separately, two of the new policy_observed tests were VACUOUS when first written (one built its own identity dict instead of reading the production literal; one called a helper instead of checking the call site) and were rewritten after induced-break testing exposed it.

notes: One exclusive file owner, including across separate worktrees.
One GPU owner across evaluation, smoke tests, warmup, profiling and backfill — held by the GPU lane; see gpu_lock_mechanism for why it was a convention plus a pgrep check rather than a lock file.
Do not mutate shared environments or active evaluator source during a run.
Use actual existing locking primitives; a ledger entry alone cannot prevent a race. A real fcntl.flock exists per run (runner.py:86) but it does not serialise two agents against DIFFERENT runs.
Before retrying a stale job, verify PID and process start time and the owned process group.
Only the lead integrates shared changes and performs final push/service verification.
